system: Cast PMMA rods concurrent flow ISS BASS-II
output: Quenching-branch minimum O2 (vol %) vs forced stretch rate a (1/s)
valid_range: a roughly 0 to 10 1/s; rod radii 0.318 0.476 0.635 cm; O2 roughly 13.5 to 22 %
fit_quality: 24 ISS tests plus drop-tower points; no R2 given
caveats: Stretch rate plotted excludes curvature-induced stretch; the authors say points shift right once curvature is included (Table 1 gives 6.0 to 8.7 1/s total for the example flames). Different minimum O2 for the 0.476 and 0.635 cm rods

system: Cast PMMA rods concurrent flow ISS BASS-II plus drop tower
output: Blowoff-branch minimum O2 (vol %) vs forced stretch rate a (1/s)
valid_range: a roughly 10 to 150 1/s; O2 roughly 13.5 to 16.5 %
fit_quality: Linear fit shown against ISS and drop-tower blowoff points; no R2 given
caveats: Extrapolating to zero stretch gives about 13.3% O2 which the authors suggest as a conservative minimum O2 for the material; extinction near the limit is stochastic

parameters: form only; coefficients not printed for the combined curve
caveats: Stochastic region rather than a sharp line. Combining BM-01 and BM-02 is my inference not a published equation

system: Kimwipes thin cellulose fuel concurrent flow 0g
equation: V = 0.2498*x + 0.4038 where x = O2_molefrac * flow_cm_s * P_atm^0.5
valid_range: O2 24 to 85 %; flow 0 to 30 cm/s (1 to 30 at 34% O2); pressure 3.6 to 14.7 psia; x roughly 0 to 12.6
fit_quality: Linear R2=0.9696 and power law R2=0.9277 (Fig 7 legend); 30 concurrent tests plus literature data (Grayson; Pettegrew)
caveats: Single fuel. Deviates from linear at very near-limit values. Sanity check: corners of the range give about 3.4 to 3.6 cm/s which matches the paper's plotted maximum

system: Kimwipes thin cellulose fuel opposed flow 0g and 1g
equation: V = 8.15*u - 1.03 where u = O2_molefrac^0.9 * P_atm^0.05 (coefficients traced from the plotted line; not printed in the paper)
parameters: slope 8.15 (+/-0.1) intercept -1.03 (+/-0.1); form is Magee and McAlevy exponents 0.9 and 0.05
valid_range: u about 0.19 to 1.0 (O2 up to 100%); flow effects not captured; the line is unreliable near the quench limit at low O2 (<40%)
fit_quality: R2=0.9536 (Fig 6 legend); 10 opposed tests plus literature data
caveats: Traced from pixels over u=0.46-0.99 and checked against the line's left end (u=0.19 gives about 0.5 cm/s as plotted). The intercept makes V negative below u=0.13 so never evaluate there. Treat as a worst-case (highest) spread-rate estimate

output: Flow velocity above which concurrent spread is faster than opposed spread
equation: Derived by equating BM-04 and BM-05
caveats: Over nearly all of the nominal spacecraft ventilation range (5 to 20 cm/s) opposed spread is faster especially in normoxic atmospheres; at 20 to 25% O2 the two are similar
